stories.headline: Empty Convoy's missing shipment can now be traced, but its reviews remain waived
stories.summary: The Empty Convoy encounter gained bounded security and a one-time custody trace with optional salvage. Its three implementation slices landed, while security and recovery independent reviews were owner-waived before launch. The latest recovery review hit a source-attestation gate, not a gameplay verdict.
stories.body: The Empty Convoy encounter progressed beyond optional placement. Security scanning now queues up to three registered enemies within ambient spawn capacity and fails safely when placement is impossible. After clearing security, the player can record an unverified shipment trace and obtain existing ruin_scrap once when the ledger supports it; otherwise evidence-only completion is preserved. C2 landed at bde08b88 and C3 at e346eaea. C2 implementation reports 10/10 selected validation checks, C3 reports 8/8. The C2 review was owner-waived without launch. C3 review was also waived before launch after the host gate rejected missing authenticated source-span provenance for the changed validation manifest. No independent PASS, gameplay acceptance or verified host teardown follows from these commits.
bullets: C2 security and C3 custody/recovery implementations landed.
Reported selected checks: C2 10/10; C3 8/8, not independent acceptance.
Both paired reviews were owner-waived prelaunch, not passed.
Host teardown and live gameplay remain unverified.

article.lead: The abandoned convoy now offers more than an eerie roadside discovery. Scanning its cargo cradle can trigger a contained defense, and surviving the encounter reveals a custody trace that refuses to pretend the missing shipment has been found. The code landed, but neither follow-up slice received independent review.

sections.heading: A threat that respects the rest of the world
sections.text: The scan queues at most three existing security units, sharing the game's ambient enemy capacity rather than creating an unlimited separate wave. If safe spawning fails, the event falls back to evidence instead of trapping the player or crashing.

sections.heading: One clue, one salvage opportunity
sections.text: After security clears, the convoy records SHIPMENT UNVERIFIED. A valid existing scrap reward may be granted once; repeated interactions and same-run reentry cannot duplicate it. Without a usable ledger entry, the clue still remains accessible.

sections.heading: The missing verdict
sections.text: Both security and recovery implementation packets landed with reported focused checks. Their paired reviews were waived before a reviewer ran. The latest review was stopped by a source-attestation requirement, so these waivers are administrative dispositions, not independent gameplay approval.

insights.title: The event chain now has a coherent playable loop
insights.explanation: Placement, bounded defense, and durable evidence form a connected interaction rather than three isolated prototypes. This creates a stronger foundation for later narrative work without asserting what happened to the cargo.

insights.title: Review waivers do not repair the proof gap
insights.explanation: The reported tests cover specific behavior, but the blocked source-attestation gate prevented independent falsification. Additional acceptance would require separately authorized review or gameplay evidence.

article.takeaway: Three Empty Convoy implementation slices are on main; security and recovery remain independently unaccepted.
article.next_watch: Watch for a separately authorized gameplay verification or an independently accepted review, not another administrative waiver.

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN's provenance tests expose a real source-inventory defect; correction lands, review still ahead
stories.summary: A focused correction to CUSTODIAN's inherited-Git-history validation uncovered and fixed a real bug: upstream-only commits before a resumed merge were counted as task-owned files. The correction landed and its packet was archived. Its newly promoted independent review remains ready, not accepted, and protected closeout stays gated.
stories.body: A user-authorized correction for independent-review finding R0-01 landed on main. Real-Git tests showed that the validator excluded the inherited merge but still counted preceding upstream-only commits as workstream-owned. The patch now authenticates the complete claim-base-to-resume history, excludes that inherited prefix from authored paths, and rejects forged or inconsistent resume evidence. The implementation summary reports 275 consumer and 89 producer tests passing. The correction packet is archived/complete, but its fresh independent review packet is ready/auto and has not returned an accepted PASS. The prior nonpassing review is unchanged. The protected summary-rename closeout remains gated. Latest GitHub repository validation and automatic handoff succeeded, while one validation run was still in progress at inspection. No canonical dispatcher audit or private operational relay observation was available; host processes, locks, worktree teardown and disk status are unknown.

article.lead: Tests intended to close a missing safety-proof gap found a real defect instead: CUSTODIAN's reviewer could mistake upstream files inherited during a task resume for files authored by that task. A narrow fix has now landed, but independent acceptance is still outstanding.

sections.heading: The bug was hiding before the merge
sections.text: The earlier correction taught CUSTODIAN to recognize a legitimate inherited Git merge. New real-repository tests revealed that the validator still included earlier upstream-only commits in its source inventory. That could misstate which files the task actually changed.

sections.heading: A bounded fix with adversarial tests
sections.text: The new implementation checks the entire inherited history between the original claim and the resume event, not just the merge itself. It verifies identity, ancestry and tree consistency, excludes inherited paths from task-owned files, and rejects tampered or contradictory resume evidence.

sections.heading: Why this is not yet an accepted closeout
sections.text: The correction landed and its implementation packet was archived. Its separate reviewer packet is ready for an independent challenge. The original review's finding remains nonpassing until that fresh review produces genuine acceptance. No local teardown or running process was verified.

insights.title: A missing test revealed a real ownership error
insights.explanation: R0-01 initially concerned absent consumer-side evidence. Adding realistic history tests exposed incorrect source attribution, showing why independent positive and adversarial cases matter beyond green unit-test totals.

insights.title: Review acceptance remains a separate gate
insights.explanation: A landed patch and archived implementation packet do not override the earlier findings verdict. The new reviewer must challenge the corrected source-inventory boundary before protected closeout can resume.

article.takeaway: The source-inventory defect is corrected on main, with fresh independent acceptance still required.
article.next_watch: Watch for a canonical independent PASS on the correction's ready reviewer packet, followed by authorized reconsideration of the protected summary-rename closeout.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has landed a correction intended to let legitimate resumed work finish without mistaking inherited upstream commits for task-authored changes. Its independent reviewer found a material gap: the new reviewer-side classification lacks focused real-Git tests. The verdict is findings, not acceptance, so the original protected closeout remains blocked.

sections.heading: A correction reaches main
sections.text: The implementation now distinguishes a merge inherited through a documented clean resume from one authored by the workstream. It checks first-parent Git ancestry, deterministic merge trees and append-only diagnostic trace evidence. The implementation was archived as complete after reported 9/9 selected validation checks passed, including focused producer and paired-review suites. Landing and passing tests do not constitute independent acceptance.

sections.heading: The reviewer identifies an untested decision
sections.text: The fresh, different-agent review found no specific bypass in the inspected code. But the independent host validator's new inherited-merge branch had no dedicated real-Git positive and negative cases proving it excludes inherited files while rejecting forged, mismatched or out-of-boundary histories. Broad test coverage does not establish that this particular authority decision was exercised. The reviewer recorded finding R0-01 and withheld PASS.

sections.heading: The original closeout remains protected
sections.text: The reviewer requests a human decision on a narrowly scoped consumer-test correction followed by fresh independent acceptance. The original canonical summary-rename finish cannot resume on the strength of this landing alone. Separately, the WIRE exporter review still needs source attestation before its private transport can proceed; no live operational relay was verified.

insights.title: A landed fix can still fail the acceptance gate
insights.explanation: The implementation has reached main and its reported tests passed, but the independent reviewer identified missing evidence for the exact new decision branch. The distinction prevents a green test suite from silently becoming permission to resume a protected claim.

insights.title: The missing tests belong to the independent consumer
insights.explanation: Producer tests exercise the completion-side rule. The host reviewer independently decides what source history to trust, so it needs its own adversarial real-Git proof that inherited changes are not misclassified as authored work.

stories.body:
CUSTODIAN has restored a valid task-packet handoff for a correction to its workstream finish machinery. A protected summary-rename job cannot close because the validator mistakes upstream history inherited during a clean resume for a merge authored by that job. stories.headline: WIRE review recovery gets an exact attestation workstream, but queue validation fails
stories.summary: A narrowly scoped implementation and independent-review pair now exists to authenticate WIRE exporter's preserved review source. Automatic handoff promoted both packets, but repository queue-authority validation and a subsequent handoff run failed. No attestation implementation, independent PASS, or transport delivery is established.
stories.body:
A new exact-source-attestation implementation/review pair was authored at 834341ab and promoted at 0e5da248. It targets the preserved exporter-review host-validation refusal, binding the proposed exception to specific source and manifest blobs, archived packet identity, reviewed main, and review run. The correction must remain inert until its own independent review is accepted.

GitHub Actions show Automatic Packet Authoring Handoff succeeded for the authored pair, but Validate Repository failed at the queue-authority gate. A subsequent handoff run on the promotion commit also failed its 'Validate and publish explicitly authorized pairs' step. These are separate failures and cannot be assumed to have the same cause. Promotion on main is not proof that the live dispatcher considers either packet claimable.

The original exporter remains landed and its preserved review is not accepted. The transport implementation/review pair remains dependency-gated; no private Dropbox observation or ChatGPT consumer readback is verified. Host worktree, lock, process and disk status were not freshly inspected.

sections.heading: A recovery bound to one source
sections.text: The new packet specifies exact implementation, archive, merge, manifest and preserved-review identities. Its proposed attestation cannot activate merely because code lands: it must pass its own independent review. That narrow scope is intended to unblock the original exporter review without weakening unrelated review safeguards.

sections.heading: Promotion does not erase failed checks

However, repository validation failed the queue-authority step, and a later automatic handoff failed on the promoted commit. Their precise causes require investigation; neither failure proves the attestation logic itself is defective.

sections.heading: The operational WIRE remains offline

stories.headline: WIRE's observation exporter lands; independent review stalls at an attestation gate
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN landed the local sanitized observation exporter and published its private-transport packet pair. The exporter passed reported focused tests, but its independent reviewer stopped at a source-attestation gate before launch. Dropbox transport remains unimplemented and dependency-blocked; a separate repository-validation run failed queue-authority checks.
stories.body:
The local WIRE observation exporter landed on main at 38545e4c12b848861284d77c299790c046df6f62. It consumes a pre-existing task-administrator snapshot, checks evidence completeness and freshness, and preserves unavailable counts rather than manufacturing zeroes. The executor reported 15 focused synthetic tests and changed-file validation passing; GitHub repository validation also passed at the landing SHA. The implementation packet was archived, but implementation testing is not independent acceptance.

The paired review was reportedly claimed as codex-reviewer and stopped by host validation before reviewer launch: 'changed validation manifest is not covered by an accepted exact source attestation.' The preserved review runs and retained worktree are host-reported, not independently inspected here. No independent PASS is established. The private transport implementation/review pair was then published and promoted on main at 8bc0fe40184dec741ccc5a92997052f96e0deb43, with implementation dependent on accepted exporter review. No private observation upload, ChatGPT retrieval, or producer schedule is established.

GitHub Actions additionally show a failed repository validation on the transport authoring commit 8967187af, specifically the task-packet queue-authority step; the automatic authoring handoff succeeded. The Godot Level Pipeline failed at the exporter landing SHA in a separate authored-level lifecycle step. These failures need separate diagnosis; neither proves the exporter itself failed.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has the first working piece of its operational reporting pipeline: a local exporter that turns an existing task-administrator snapshot into a constrained, sanitized observation. The code has landed, but a separate evidence-authentication rule stopped its independent reviewer before review could begin. The private Dropbox delivery layer must wait.

sections.heading: What the exporter changes
sections.text: Instead of inferring project activity from GitHub branches, the exporter is designed to consume an existing operational snapshot and report only supported counts. It rejects stale or inconsistent evidence and keeps missing values unknown. That is the foundation for a more truthful WIRE status panel, but it is not a live telemetry service yet.

sections.heading: Why the review cannot proceed
sections.text: The reviewer was stopped by a host-validation requirement for an accepted exact source attestation covering the changed validation manifest. Passing implementation tests cannot substitute for this proof. The preserved claim and review evidence need a supported recovery, not a bypass.

sections.heading: Transport is queued, not operating
sections.text: A separate implementation and independent-review pair for private Dropbox delivery has been promoted. Its implementation explicitly depends on accepted exporter review. No upload or ChatGPT readback has been verified. Separately, a repository validation run failed a packet queue-authority check on the transport authoring commit; that failure should be diagnosed rather than conflated with exporter test results.

insights.title: The bottleneck has shifted from code to provenance
insights.explanation: The exporter has landed and reported tests pass. The immediate obstacle is proving the exact reviewed source and validation policy to the independent review system. Resolving that gate unlocks the transport dependency without weakening the acceptance contract.

insights.title: A ready packet is not an active data pipeline
insights.explanation: The transport pair exists in the queue, but its dependency is unmet and there is no verified upload, consumer retrieval, or schedule. WIRE must continue labeling GitHub-only observations as partial.

article.takeaway: The exporter is landed, but the independent-review and private-delivery milestones remain open. Treat the source-attestation recovery as the next gate.
article.next_watch: Watch for a supported source-attestation recovery plan and genuine independent PASS, plus a separate diagnosis of the queue-authority CI failure.
